thread:
megan_support: FYI customer ACME reported a burst of 5xx/timeout errors against hosted /v1/generate from 03:12–03:18 UTC. They saw ~40% error rate for ~6min. No global alerts fired. Opening a quick war-room.
opsbot: incident created — ID INC-6880 — severity: high — participants paged.
alex_eng: I can join. Any repro data? request ids?
megan_support: Pasted a short curl customer used: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-medium\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'` -> 502/504s. Customer attached 5 request-ids: rid=acme-23f, acme-24g, acme-24h, acme-25a, acme-25b.
rishi_sre: Checking ingress/gateway logs now. Initial signal: proxy returned 502 with upstream error code proxy_connect_failure. No backend OOMs in that window.
jamal_infra: Not seeing GPU pool pressure spikes. Host-level metrics normal. But I do see a spike in auth service latency around 03:11–03:15 UTC (p90 auth latency ~1.8s -> normally 120ms).
alex_eng: If auth is slow it could push request timeouts and open connections in the gateway, causing 502s. Do we have auth retry/backoff behavior in the edge path?
rishi_sre: Edge retries are conservative (1 retry) but we have a short overall handshake timeout for upstreams. If auth stalls, downstream request can hit circuit break.
jamal_infra: I pushed a temporary routing policy to bypass centralized auth for ACME (token was validated earlier via cached session) — routing to a guarded path that skips remote KMS call. Doing this to confirm auth latency is the driver.
opsbot: deploy policy applied by jamal_infra: bypass-auth-for-tenant=acme (safe-guarded).
megan_support: Customer reports errors dropped to ~2% immediately after routing change. They confirm better success rate.
claire_product: Good quick mitigation. We need a postmortem and clear customer comms. Also check billing/KMS rate limiting — that auth spike smelled like a downstream KMS throttle.
anjal_eng: (typo) — ignore
alex_eng: rishi — can you pull traces for one of the request IDs? want to see span timing (edge -> auth -> runtime).
rishi_sre: Pasted trace snippet: `edge_span -> auth_call (1.9s) -> auth-kms: 1.2s wait -> auth service retries 2x -> runtime connection attempt 120ms -> gateway abort`. Looks like auth->kms backend was the long pole.
jamal_infra: KMS reported a transient rate limit at 03:10–03:16 UTC in eu-west region (throttles on customer-managed KMS integration). That matches.
megan_support: ACME uses customer-managed encryption keys via our KMS integration. They reached a short burst during a batch job they ran.
claire_product: That explains why it didn't show global GPU issues. This is tenant-scoped. For mitigation we: 1) routed tenant to cached-validate path (done), 2) temporarily increased upstream timeouts for gateway to avoid aborts on slow auth while fallback engages (jamal PR), 3) offered ACME a dedicated capacity option while they fix KMS bursts.
alex_eng: We also introduced a soft-fallback: if auth KMS is slow, allow validated cached-tokens for N minutes to avoid operator-visible 5xx. Needs security review.
rishi_sre: Agree on soft-fallback but must log audit and surface to ops. I've added a trace tag auth_fallback=true when that path runs so we can query later.
megan_support: Customer asked for timeline and root cause. I told them we mitigated by routing and are investigating KMS throttles. Would like a concise postmortem and action items to share.
jamal_infra: Action items I can pick up: - revert bypass once KMS fixed (owner jamal_infra) - add gateway config flag to allow tenant-level fallback window (owner jamal_infra) - add a synthetic test that exercises KMS-backed auth at scale (owner jamal_infra).
claire_product: Product/Support items: - draft customer-facing summary + timeline (owner megan_support) - evaluate offering temporary dedicated capacity / reserved path for affected customers (owner claire_product) - assess policy for default fallback allowances (sec consult) (owner claire_product).
alex_eng: Engineering/Runtime: - add telemetry: per-tenant auth latency histogram + alerting (owner alex_eng) - instrument retry/backoff logic visibility in tracing (owner alex_eng) - run a security review on cached-token fallback (owner alex_eng & rishi_sre).
rishi_sre: I'll write the initial postmortem skeleton and attach logs/traces. Also creating a pager alert rule: if tenant auth p90 > 1s and corresponding 5xx rate > 5% in 5m, page oncall.
opsbot: note added to INC-6880: postmortem-draft created by rishi_sre.
megan_support: Customer follow-up scheduled for 15:00 UTC. I'll include proposed action items and offer dedicated pool as stopgap.
jamal_infra: quick config we rolled: `gateway.upstream.timeout_ms=15000` for tenant=acme (was 5000). We should review global impact — change is tenant-scoped.
alex_eng: Please add a short-term monitoring dashboard (per-tenant 5xx, auth latency, KMS error rate). We need visibility before next burst.
claire_product: Timeline for action items? Recommend 72h for telemetry + alerts, 7d for fallback policy and security review, 14d for synthetic test + dedicated pool playbook.
megan_support: Noted. I'll share that timeline with the customer and link to postmortem when available.
jamal_infra: Will also add a small playbook note: when customer-managed KMS is detected and tenant 5xx spike present, toggle cached-validate route and notify SRE.
alex_eng: Are there any downstream billing concerns? If KMS is customer-managed they bear rate limits; but we should surface guidance in docs about key usage patterns.
claire_product: Agreed — docs task: add KMS rate guideline + recommended quotas for high-throughput workloads. Owner: claire_product.
megan_support: Closing war-room now. Summary for thread: root cause = customer-managed KMS throttling -> auth latency -> gateway upstream aborts -> 5xx for tenant. Mitigation = tenant bypass to cached validation + increased tenant upstream timeout. Action items assigned. Posting postmortem draft link in INC-6880.
opsbot: channel archived for incident INC-6880.
